'''John Edwin Field FRS'''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Walley|first=Stephen M.|last2=Proud|first2=William G.|last3=Leighton|first3=Timothy G.|date=2021|title=John Edwin Field. 20 September 1936—21 October 2020|url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2021.0013|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=71}}</ref> (20 September 1936 – 21 October 2020) was a British experimental [[physicist]] whose research focused on the physics and chemistry of solids, particularly involving energetic phenomena and [[Materials science|materials]], covering a variety of topics from [[erosion]] to [[explosive]]s.

Following his undergraduate studies in physics at [[University College London]], Field moved to the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], undertaking his PhD in the Physics and Chemistry of Solids Group. He remained at Cambridge for the rest of his career which included terms as Head of the Physics and Chemistry of Solids Group and Deputy Head of the Cavendish Laboratory. He was also a Fellow of [[Magdalene College, Cambridge|Magdalene College]].

His achievements were recognised by an [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] in 1987 and Fellowship of [[Royal Society|the Royal Society]] in 1994.
